class.name: NetwGroupPromise
class.brief_description: The pending results of a one-to-many broadcast request, one entry per responding peer.
class.description: [method Netw.request_all] returns one of these after fanning a request out to every live peer. The awaited set is snapshotted at send time, so a peer that joins mid-flight is not waited on, and a peer that disconnects is dropped from the set so the group can still complete. [method then] fires once with the full [code]peer_id -> value[/code] map when the last response lands, while [signal completed_single] reports each response as it arrives. [codeblock] Netw.request_all(player.ready_check) \ .then(func(votes: Dictionary) -> void: start_when_all_ready(votes) ) [/codeblock] On timeout the group settles through [method catch_error] with [constant @GlobalScope.ERR_TIMEOUT], and whatever responses arrived first remain readable on [member results]. It settles exactly once, whichever way it goes, and chaining after it settled fires the callback immediately, so there is no race between sending and subscribing. It shares the settle vocabulary of [NetwPromise], which is the one-to-one form. The two are siblings rather than a base and a subclass: a group's answer is a map and a promise's is a value, and nothing reads them through one type.

method.name: answer
method.description: What the batch settled with, as one value: [member results] when every peer arrived and [member code] when it failed. This is what [signal ready] carries, so one channel answers both outcomes.

method.name: catch_error
method.description: Chains [param cb] to run when the group fails or times out, receiving [member code] and [member detail]. A group that already failed runs it immediately.

method.name: create
method.description: A group awaiting exactly [param peers]. An empty set is already satisfied and is deliberately NOT settled here, because nothing has subscribed yet: whoever hands the group to a caller settles it at their session's next settle, which is the first moment the caller can have chained onto it.

method.name: reject
method.description: Settles the group as failed. Emits [signal failed] then [signal settled] and runs every chained [method catch_error]. A group that already settled is unchanged.

method.name: remove_peer
method.description: Drops [param peer_id] from the awaited set without recording an answer for it, which is what a disconnect during the flight does. Settles the group when it was the last one awaited.

method.name: resolve_all
method.description: Settles the group as completed with whatever [member results] holds. Emits [signal completed] then [signal settled] and runs every chained [method then].

method.name: resolve_peer
method.description: Records [param peer_id]'s answer and emits [signal completed_single]. Settles the group when it was the last one awaited. A peer the group is not awaiting answers for nobody: it records nothing and settles nothing, because the awaited set is the snapshot the group promised over and a late arrival is not part of it.

method.name: then
method.description: Chains [param cb] to run when every awaited peer has answered, receiving the [member results] map. A group that already completed runs it immediately.

method.name: wait
method.description: Answers a [Signal] on the [signal ready] channel that is safe to [code]await[/code] whether or not the batch has already settled, carrying [method answer]. This is the idiom. Awaiting [signal completed] directly is a race the caller cannot win: a batch whose peers all resolved before the wait has already emitted it, and the caller waits forever. An already-settled batch defers its emission here, so the [code]await[/code] subscribes before the answer is delivered. [codeblock] await destination.move_participants(peers).wait() [/codeblock] This never re-emits [signal completed], [signal failed] or [signal settled], so an earlier subscriber is notified exactly once no matter how late anyone waits.

members.member: The settle code when [member is_failed], otherwise [constant @GlobalScope.OK].
The human-readable reason behind [member code], empty when the code says it all. Diagnostics only, never a branch condition.
The peers still owed an answer, in the order the group was created with.
Whether the request failed or timed out.
Whether the group settled, whichever way it went.
The [code]peer_id -> result[/code] map of every answer received so far, readable before the group settles and after it fails.

signal.name: completed
signal.description: Emitted once every awaited peer has resolved.

signal.name: completed_single
signal.description: Emitted as each awaited peer resolves, before the group itself settles.

signal.name: failed
signal.description: Emitted when the group is rejected by a timeout or a failure.

signal.name: ready
signal.description: The channel [method wait] answers on, carrying [method answer]. A pending batch emits it once on its settle edge, so every waiter is answered by that one emission. A batch that already settled emits it once per [method wait] call, deferred, so a late caller is answered rather than left waiting. [b]Note:[/b] connect to [signal settled] instead. Because a settled batch emits this per call, a subscriber attached by hand can see it more than once. [method wait] is its only intended producer and consumer.

signal.name: settled
signal.description: Emitted once the group settled, whichever way it went, after [signal completed] or [signal failed].
